channel.title: The Western Producer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Western Producer (producer.com)

item.title: Open sow housing deadline may prove difficult
item.description: Fifty to 60 per cent of sows on the Prairies are now housed in open systems, says a designer of housing and feeding systems for livestock. Getting the rest across the finish line will be a struggle.

item.title: Young farmers urged to start smart, invest now
item.description: Investing is commonly perceived as something for the future, like retirement, that isn’t at the top of mind for young farmers, but it should be.

item.title: Bayer proposes $7.25 billion plan to settle U.S. Roundup cancer suits
item.description: Bayer said on Tuesday its Monsanto unit had filed a proposed U.S. class settlement totalling as much as $7.25 billion (C$9.89 billion) aimed at resolving all current and future claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused cancer.

item.title: Pulse Weekly: Lentil prices currently lacking direction
item.description: There’s little at the present time to guide cash prices for lentils on the Canadian Prairies, said Marcos Mosnaim of Prairie IX in Toronto.

item.title: As U.S. agriculture flails, farmers see big corn acres as best bet to break even
item.description: U.S. farmers are expected to only cut back slightly on corn acres as it nears break-even prices and seems less politically risky than soybeans.

item.title: Mexico updates import requirements for Eastern Canadian apples
item.description: Mexico has updated rules around imports of apples from Eastern Canada, a move the Canadian Food Inspection Agency says will reduce costs for Canadian exporters.

item.title: Prairie producers try to meet rising lamb demand
item.description: Sheep markets in Saskatchewan and Alberta can’t keep up with the demand for lamb.

item.title: India expected to increase its lentil import duty
item.description: AgPulse Analytica expects India to hike its lentil duty to 30 per cent as of April 1.

item.title: Cash incentive for CRSB Certified beef producers launched
item.description: The Canadian Roundtable for Sustainable Beef (CRSB) has launched an incentive payment for CRSB Certified producers.

item.title: Top potash producer Nutrien misses fourth-quarter profit estimates
item.description: Nutrien missed analysts’ expectations for fourth-quarter profit on Wednesday, as lower sales in its crop nutrients business weighed on the world’s top potash producer.
